Isn't every transaction traceable? I'd like my Money 2.0 to be anonymous.

Every transaction can be traced to an address, yes. But first, whoever wants to trace your transactions is going to have to work at it, hard. And even when they have linked an address to someone's identity, all that can be proven is that money has moved around. What matters is what a nefarious agent can do about you spending or earning Bitcoins, and that's nothing. Right now, whenever money comes in or out of your bank account, where the money goes and which account receives it is documented, not to mention your access to your own bank account is limited depending on the time of day and whether regulators agree/disagree with your lifestyle. While I agree perfect anonymity would be optimal, having a digital form of money that can't be replicated, hacked, stolen, shut down, or prohibited from moving is a damned good place to start.

What about the enormous energy consumption?

This is a legitimate question and I will try to convince you why Bitcoin mining as it stands is a very good thing. You ask anyone in the business of outputting value using machinery what they wish they could afford and it'd be more efficiency. Any businessman serious about staying competitive will tell you they want smaller machines that crank out more value at a lower cost. Look back to computers of the 70s, those things were the size of present day stoves. Now, a computer fits in the palm (almost) of your hand. We are looking at the possibility of a beneficial arms race to humanity, a computational arms race that will result in everyone benefiting from the implications. Mining in its current form won't last long. Developers and engineers are working to make a more efficient yet powerful Bitcoin miners, and anyone who wants to keep profiting from the endeavor will need to switch their equipment to keep up with the pack. Moore's law is projected to remain relevant for at least 7 more years (and a lot could happen in 7 years).

Here is the part where I use the previous logic and apply it to a more potent way of conserving energy as well as extracting it from our environment. So in closing, as long as there is competition, there will be increased efficiency, and that is good.

I am actually an antinatalist. Not saying this to be controversial, I have thought that breeding is immoral for at least 4 years now.

As for reasons why, I can't be bothered typing stuff out again, so here's a link to an old blog of mine I used to post about antinatalist stuff on after my teenage suicide attempt. My main reason is that I don't think it should be at all allowed for people to gamble on lives that aren't even their own, by having a child that could come to such suffering, some of this suffering a direct result of the parents themselves (genetics, abusive childhood etc.) and some nonetheless (torture etc.) still a result of the parents, because the child wouldn't have had a potential life not worth living as a result of the parents.

I will vehemently uphold my stance on this, but I only tell people to see if they are the kind of person who would become an antinatalist as well. Arguing, I have learnt, doesn't actually work (although in general, not just on antinatalism, I don't think arguing works as people, including me probably, never change their views so I try not to do it):

That is a pretty fascinating philosophy. Forgive my ignorance, I don't know much about it. But are you not perhaps skewed towards this philosophy from your depression or is there more to it than that? Personally I would prefer to have existed, lived, suffered and pondered the universe than not. Most of the rest of the universe has no life / intelligence and ability to reflect on it's existence. It's our curse AND our blessing in my opinion.

Oh no don't worry about not knowing about it, it is SERIOUSLY niche, very few people on earth I'd wager know about it. It probably only really exists because of the internet, in my opinion. I am definitely skewed towards it because of my mental illness. But when I think about it now, it's not associated with my depressed feelings, but rather with my outrage that few care about people like me, who suffer enough to feel life is not worth living. This is not a recent thought. My life is slightly tolerable now and I'm not at risk from suicide or even self-harm. But because of anhedonia (loss of pleasure/joy caused by depression), for at least 5 years now I have felt little but suffering and emptiness. Before that I did feel a good amount of joy in life, but still had daily suicidal thoughts due to anxiety, bullying and neglectful parents.

I've met other people who wish they had never been born. They generally tend to agree with this sort of philosophy - because they think that just because other people would have preferred to be born if they had had a choice, that that doesn't justify them being born, who not only would prefer not to, but who underwent immense suffering because their parents decided to bring them into the world. It's said that people who have good lives make the bad lives okay somehow, but people who don't exist don't benefit from being born and feeling good. But people who do exist and suffer ARE hurt by being born, so therefore no benefit + hurting people in my opinion means antinatalism.

Sorry about kind of rambling arguments, my blog in general is a lot better thought out.
